newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kia Group pleads for continuing credit.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kia Group pleads for continuing credit.

text.p: The head of South Korea's Kia Group has asked finance minister Kang Kyong-shik to persuade merchant banks to maintain the group's credit lines, the group said in Tuesday in a statment.
Group chairman Kim Sun-hong also was quoted as saying Kia affiliates would seek restructuring to improve their financial status, it said.
The statement said chairman Kim told minister Kang that the group was suffering from a liquidity shortage because of continuing "malicious rumours".
"Currently, Kia has no managerial problems at all. But the bad rumours about deteriorating financial problems are damaging us," Kim was quoted as saying.
He said the contention that the nation's crowded car industry may need restructuring also fueled concerns about the group.
Some 5,000 sub-contractors and 4,000 overseas sales outlets feared serious impacts because of the situation, the statement said.
A domestic newpaper said minister Kang was quoted as saying the government would support Kia's efforts to normalise its management.
"It makes no sense that such sound enterprises as Kia should go bankrupt," Kang was quoted as saying.

Asia Motors, a Kia unit which makes commercial vehicles, would raise about 520 billion won by moving its plant to a cheaper site two to three years ahead of schedule, Kim was quoted in the statement as saying.
Kim also said the group planned to sell off some 795 billion won worth of idle assets.
